articles.title: Knowing Is Not Telling: Identity Ossification in LLM Representations of Trans-border Communities
articles.summary: arXiv:2610.12610v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Ethnic and cultural identities rarely align with political borders, a tension made sharper by migration and long-standing cross-border ties. Communities such as the Sami, the Rohingya, and the Kurds have long lived across more than one state. This tension is especially clear in mainland Southeast Asia, where many communities share history, language, and culture across state lines. articles.summary: arXiv:2610.12792v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Technologies like large language models make it easier to convert cultural material into analyzable variables, while LLM-driven agentic systems extend machine assistance to other parts of the research workflow. articles.title: Developing Competency in AI Ethics: A training framework
articles.summary: arXiv:2610.13319v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present a training framework for developing core competencies in the practical operationalisation of AI ethics: (1) identifying ethical concerns; (2) determining which standard ethics requirements they implicate; (3) selecting and prioritising concrete technical and organisational measures to address them; and (4) recognising ethics tensions and reasoning about trade-offs where such tensions cannot be fully resolved. articles.title: Adversarial Attacks Reveal Divergent Deception Competence in Humans and Generative Language Models
articles.summary: arXiv:2610.13363v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Machine learning models typically outperform humans in deception detection. A threat to machine learning models is their vulnerability to adversarial attacks: subtle yet targeted perturbations of input data that trick a model into misclassification. Yet, this also provides an opportunity: understanding how humans versus machines construct attacks offers new insights into second-order beliefs about deception. articles.summary: arXiv:2610.12701v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Perspectivist NLP has established that annotator positionality shapes labels for subjective tasks, but the field still lacks methods for operationalising it. articles.title: The False Allure of "Security by Obscurity": A Game-Theoretic Approach
articles.summary: arXiv:2610.12858v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: "Security by obscurity," or the idea that hiding how a system works helps protect it from adversaries, has long been poorly regarded in the security community. Yet its intuitive appeal persists, and it has resurfaced repeatedly in industry practices and public debates over the years. articles.title: Beyond the Monolithic Interface: A Research Agenda for Plural Conversational AI
articles.summary: arXiv:2610.12878v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The current paradigm of artificial intelligence (AI) design elevates conversational chatbot interfaces, making them the default mode through which hundreds of millions of people interact with AI systems globally.
